# C and C++

C makes the smallest and fastest modules: the summary example is 25 KB, its first call compiles in about 17 ms, and later calls load it from the cache in half a millisecond. The easiest compiler is `zig cc`: Zig ships clang and wasi-libc together, so there's no SDK to install.

## Set up

```bash
brew install zig   # or download it from ziglang.org
```

Clang with [wasi-sdk](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasi-sdk) works too: replace `zig cc -target wasm32-wasi` below with `$WASI_SDK_PATH/bin/clang --target=wasm32-wasip1`.

## The module

[`example/summary/c`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/c/main.c) counts the words of a text and returns the first twelve. C has no JSON in its standard library, so it takes the text as it is (your code can pass a string) and prints JSON:

```c
// what `summary --describe` prints: manifest.json, built in (C23 #embed)
static const char manifest[] = {
#embed "manifest.json"
    , 0};

static void fail(const char *code, const char *message) {
  fprintf(stderr, "{\"code\":\"%s\",\"message\":\"%s\"}", code, message);
  exit(1);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  const char *function = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "";
  if (strcmp(function, "--describe") == 0) {
    fputs(manifest, stdout);
    return 0;
  }
  if (strcmp(function, "run") != 0) fail("no_such_function", "only run");

  // read stdin, count the words, keep the first 12 ...

  fputs("{\"text\":", stdout);
  put_json_string(short_text, m);
  printf(",\"words\":%zu}", words);
  return 0;
}
```

To take JSON in, add a parser such as [cJSON](https://github.com/DaveGamble/cJSON) (one `.c` file and a header) beside `main.c` and list it on the command line.

## Build

```bash
zig cc -target wasm32-wasi -std=c23 -Os -s -Wl,-z,stack-size=1048576 \
  -o pb_hooks/summary.pb.wasm main.c
```

- `-Os -s`: smallest code, no symbols.
- `-Wl,-z,stack-size=1048576`: a 1 MB stack. Without it, `zig cc` gives a WASI program a 16 MB stack, and every call would start with 16 MB of memory.
- `-std=c23`: for `#embed`. Without it, keep the manifest in a string instead.

## Call it

An API route that saves a post with its summary and word count:

```ts
// pb_pages/posts.ts
export async function post(ctx: any) {
  const { body } = ctx.req.body()
  const out = await $wasm.run.async<{ text: string; words: number }>("summary", String(body ?? "")) // a string goes in as it is
  const record = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId("posts"))
  record.load({ body, summary: out.text, words: out.words })
  ctx.app.save(record)
  return ctx.res.json(201, { id: record.id, summary: out.text, words: out.words })
}
```

## C++

`zig c++` builds C++ the same way, with `-fno-exceptions` added:

```bash
zig c++ -target wasm32-wasi -fno-exceptions -Os -s -Wl,-z,stack-size=1048576 \
  -o pb_hooks/mymodule.pb.wasm main.cpp
```

WebAssembly exception handling doesn't run here, so code that throws, the standard library's included, fails to link (`undefined symbol: __cxa_throw`) until exceptions are off. What you use of the standard library sets the size: a program that uses `std::string` and `printf` is 20 KB, one that reads stdin with iostreams 204 KB.

## Libraries

C libraries that only compute (parsers, codecs, compression, math) usually build as they are: add their `.c` files to the command. What WASI preview 1 doesn't have fails to build or fails at run time: threads, sockets, `fork`, and files (no folder is mounted, so `fopen` fails).
